Research relevant laws, regulations and policies and develops appropriate historical information relating to program accomplishments and as necessary, recommends further study and analysis.
Assess and identifies administrative areas needing further policy guidance or interpretation.

Keep fully appraised of new and changed administrative policies and procedures affecting the various staff elements of the ODCS, G-8, and develops implementing instructions and guidance for determination.

Provide advice and guidance to the Directors and staff on appropriate procedural policies in the preparation of presentations to the G-8 or for those occasions when ODCS, G-8 staff represents the G-8 to other agencies.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: A. RESUME BASED--EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (NTE 5 Pages): A well-written resume will demonstrate to the Hiring Official that you possess the ECQs and associated competencies: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/senior-executive-service/reference-materials/guidetosesquals_2012.pdf 1) Leading Change: Competencies: Creativity and Innovation, External Awareness, Flexibility, Resilience, Strategic Thinking, and Vision 2) Leading People: Competencies: Conflict Management , Leveraging Diversity, Developing Others and Team Building 3) Results Driven: Competencies: Accountability, Customer Service, Decisiveness, Entrepreneurship, Problem Solving and Technical Credibility 4) Business Acumen: Competencies: Financial Management, Human Capital Management and Technology Management 5) Building Coalitions: Competencies: Partnering, Political Savvy and Influencing/Negotiating Helpful Tips: - Quantify accomplishments and be sure to include the scope on every example (the number of staff/employees, budget, cost savings, and nature of work) - Use active words such as led, instructed, tasked, facilitated, assigned, and/or assembled others to achieve the goals and mission of the organization - Spell out and limit the use of acronyms B. MANDATORY TECHNICAL QUALIFICATIONS (MTQs): (NTE 2 pages - PDF format) A supplemental statement must be submitted separately addressing each MTQ. Recommend applicant submit 1 page per MTQ, not exceeding 2 pages total for both MTQs. MTQs must provide specific examples that address relevant experience and accomplishments. Applicants should focus on recent experience, education, and training, as some Recruitment Panel and Executive Resources Board members may consider experience that's over 10 years old to be outdated. Applicants must reflect superior technical qualifications demonstrated through leadership and management in the following: (Recommend applying the CCAR Format - Challenge, Context, Actions and Results as you write your narrative responses) 1. Resource and Fiscal Management - provides all levels of budget analysis, budget construction, program objective memorandum (POM) development and interaction with Combatant Commands, MAJCOMs, agencies, Joint Staff and Office of Secretary of Defense (OSD) on all Air Force budget programming issues. The incumbent assists in the development, justification, and defense of the Air Force Budget Estimate Submission (BES) and the President's Budget (PB). Determines the impact of Congressional marks and legislations on Air Force programs and makes recommendations to the Air Force Corporate Structure in alignment with strategic priorities. 2. Provide AF Senior Leadership with programming analyses, evaluations, and recommendations on programmatic and budgetary issues associated with the development, submission, and defense of the $822B AF POM to OSD. Develop and evaluate options relating to USAF force structure, readiness, sustainability and modernization for the Secretary and Chief of Staff of the Air Force. In addition, DoD requires an Enterprise Perspective. The individual must possess a broad point of view and an awareness and understanding of individual or organizational responsibilities in relation to DoD or government-wide strategic priorities. Executives should demonstrate ability to work with internal and external partners to support national security objectives. This perspective is typically gained through a variety of diverse work experiences. A separate narrative statement is not required--this information should be embedded within the application package [Resume (not to exceed 5 pages) and Technical Qualifications (not to exceed a combined total of 2 pages)]. DESIRED ATTRIBUTES: The Deputy Director should possess a broad knowledge of the basic principles and practices of programming, program planning, financial management, manpower policy and planning, organizational planning, strategic and long-range planning, personnel management, quality, and executive administration. The Deputy Director should possess expert knowledge of specific OSD and Air Force procedures and directives regarding programming and program planning, strategic and long-range planning, and manpower and organizational planning; and a full understanding of DoD and Air Force organization and working relationships. The Deputy Director should have the ability to quickly grasp complex scientific and engineering concepts, and an understanding of the programmatic and policy issues faced by Program Element Monitors, and functional, technical, and budget analysts. The Deputy Director should display a high level of initiative in resolving complex issues and an exceptional degree of tact in dealing with senior officials. Position requires access to TOP SECRET and SPECIAL ACCESS information. The Deputy Director develops annual Programming Guidance in accordance with overarching National and Defense guidance, policy, and objectives. Incumbent reviews, develops, and evaluates proposed options to change the Air Force Program prior to, during, and following periods of major exercises to determine impacts on balance, integration, and mission areas. The Deputy Director prepares senior Air Force leadership for advocacy and defense of the Air Force Program, and establishes Air Force resource allocation and Planning, Programming and Budgeting Execution (PPBE) policy. The incumbent functions as the Associate Deputy Director for Programs Office of Primary Responsibility for all matters pertaining to developing, directing, and conducting Air Force programming activities. When directed, the Deputy Director will co-chair the Air Force Board in the absence of the Director.

Details.JobSummary: This position is located in the Director of Programs (AF/ A8P), Deputy Chief of Staff for Plans and Programs (AF/A8), Pentagon, Washington, DC. This position serves as the Deputy Director for Programs. The Deputy Director for Programs assists and advises the Director of Programs (AF/A8P) in all aspects of AF/A8P functions. Click on "Learn more about this agency" button below for IMPORTANT additional information.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is to fly, fight and win...airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Reach and Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do. SALARY: $171,268.00 - $195,000.00 per annum. (Air Force Tier 1) SES members are eligible for performance based annual salary increases and/or bonuses in addition to an annual salary. AREA OF CONSIDERATION: Applications will be accepted from all qualified persons. This is a SES Career Reserved position and is assigned a precedence priority code of DV-6/ Brig Gen, Tier 1 for protocol purposes. MOBILITY: Organizational and geographical mobility is essential in developing and managing SES and DISES leaders and generally is a key to advancement. Therefore, mobility is a condition of employment and appointed SES and DISES members will be required to sign a Reassignment Rights and Obligation Agreement.
MajorDuties: This position is located in the Director of Programs (AF/A8P), Deputy Chief of Staff for Plans and Programs (AF/A8), Pentagon, Washington, DC. This position serves as the Deputy Director for Programs. The Associate Deputy for Programs assists and advises the Director of Programs (AF/A8P) in all aspects of AF/A8P functions. The Deputy Director for Programs assists the Director for Programs in the performance of the Directorate's mission. AF/A8P develops, integrates, evaluates, and analyzes the $605 billion USAF Future Years Defense Program. AF/A8P develops and evaluates options relating to force structure, readiness, sustainability, and modernization for the Secretary of the Air Force and Chief of Staff of the Air Force. The Deputy Director performs these duties in the absence of the Director. The Deputy Director develops annual Programming Guidance in accordance with overarching National and Defense guidance, policy, and objectives. Incumbent reviews, develops, and evaluates proposed options to change the Air Force Program prior to, during, and following periods of major exercises to determine impacts on balance, integration, and mission areas. The Associate prepares senior Air Force leadership for advocacy and defense of the Air Force Program, and establishes Air Force resource allocation and Planning, Programming and Budgeting Execution (PPBE) policy. The incumbent functions as the Associate Deputy Director for Programs Office of Primary Responsibility for all matters pertaining to developing, directing, and conducting Air Force programming activities. When directed, the Associate will co-chair the Air Force Board in the absence of the Director. The incumbent maintains the integrity of the corporate process, and provides information and briefings to the Corporate Structure for corporate decisions. The Associate coordinates with SAF/FMB to develop Future Years Defense Plan (FYDP), and produces program change guidance. Determines how Air Force Strategy, Planning Choices, and Programming affect the AF budget and ensure budget activities align with strategy. Incumbent performs analyses which assess program capabilities and program compliance with fiscal and force structure guidance. Reviews and evaluates impacts caused by changes to the Air Force Program. Evaluates historical trends compared with current FYDP (by appropriation, mission areas, etc.). Tracks areas of recurring external challenges to the Air Force Budget and identifies likely Budget Review and Program Review Issues. The Deputy Director analyzes fiscal guidance from the Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD). Evaluates the distribution of DoD fiscal resources (funding and real growth) for DoD, Air Force, and other Services. Helps assess the Air Force's compliance with program guidance provided by OSD and Air Force leadership, and evaluates the programmatic impact of those changes made to the Air Force Program.
Details.Education: A bachelor's degree from an accredited institution is highly desired. A master's or advanced degree in Business or National Security Studies/Affairs is highly desired

If you do not provide an email address, you are responsible for checking status updates and notifications in USAJOBS. Hard copy notifications will not be sent to you.
Details.RequiredDocuments: To receive full consideration, each applicant must submit the documents in the format as designated. Packages that do not include all of the required documents or meet format requirements will not be forwarded for consideration. **************ALL DOCUMENTS MUST BE UPLOADED IN PDF FORMAT******************* The Qualifications Documents must be formatted using Times New Roman, size 12 font, with 1-inch margins. Do not use borders, provide photos, or list a Social Security Number on any of the Qualifications Documents. DO NOT COMBINE DOCUMENTS. A. A resume-based application method will be used. Do NOT submit traditional ECQ narratives. Instead, applicants are required to submit a resume, not to exceed 5 pages, that shows possession of the ECQs. (See preferred format below). Upload in PDF format. PLEASE DO NOT USE USAJOBS RESUME BUILDER B. Mandatory Technical Qualifications Statement addressing each of the MTQs. Your MTQs must not exceed a combined total of 2 pages. Upload in PDF format and include the MTQ statement as indicated in the announcement (or indicate MTQ 1/MTQ 2). C. Most recent completed Performance Appraisal (current and/or former federal employees) or Performance Report (OPR or EPR). MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-12, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience include: (1) designing and conducting comprehensive studies, and developing solutions to broad, important, and severe organizational structure and program administration procedures; (2) strategic planning methods, concepts, strategy alignment and enterprise performance management; (3) planning, organizing, and developing studies or projects, and to negotiate effectively with management to accept and implement recommendations, where the proposals involve substantial resources, and require extensive changes in established concepts and procedures; (4) knowledge of business case analysis approaches and techniques, and performing multi-factor evaluation. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in­-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-12 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-13 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Knowledge of the principles, functions, and processes of project management. Knowledge and experience in Information Technology implementation. 2. Knowledge of the organization, programs, missions, and functions of Air Force organizations to conduct studies to determine manning and skill levels and make recommendations on use of personnel resources. 3. Knowledge of the manpower and personnel data systems and familiarity with computer procedures to retrieve and use information. Requires the ability to use a personal computer. 4. Skill in gathering, assembling, and analyzing facts; drawing conclusions; devising solutions to problems; identifying changes and trends; and preparing and presenting briefings and reports. 5. Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, to gain cooperation from others through tact, courtesy, and diplomacy. 6. Ability to plan, organize, and work independently within a small to medium sized organization. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.JobSummary: Click on "Learn more about this agency" button below to view Eligibilities being considered and other IMPORTANT information. The primary purpose of this position is to as a 38P Career Field and Organizational Policy Officer at the Air Staff level responsible for development and application of USAF-wide career field and organizational philosophy, objectives, principles and policies. Applies this knowledge to USAF-wide organizational and management problems and develops problem solutions.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is: To fly, fight, and win ... Airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Global Reach and Global Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do. Click here to view the AF Civilian Employment Eligibility Guide: 30 Percent or More Disabled Veterans AF DCIPS Interchange AF Internal Employee DoD Transfer (Excluding Air Force) EO 12721 Certain Former Overseas Employees EO 13473 Appointment of Certain Military Spouses Former Federal Employees (Reinstatement) Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan Land Management Employee Military Spouse Preference National Service (Peace Corps and VISTA) Non-AF DCIPS Interchange Non-Appropriated Fund Non-DoD Transfer Other (Interchange Agreements) People with Disabilities, Schedule A Veterans Employment Opportunities Act
MajorDuties: Analyzes and develops organizational initiatives, applying established organizational policies and principals to assess the impact of proposed changes on the affected activity and other major Air Force structures. Leads, develops, coordinates, recommends, and carries out studies for strategic policy, planning and analysis initiatives for Air Force A1 programs primarily focused on civilian and military career field design; organizational design, structure, and development. Develops and coordinates long-range strategic plans for the career field's human capital management of the total force (active duty, reserve, and civilian). Represents the Directorate with a variety of organizations in all matters related to assigned project areas. Prepares reports, briefings submissions, justifications and background papers. Integrates IT programming and planning with projects, plans, and requirements. Manages, updates, organizes community integrated SharePoint web site.
Details.Education: This job does not have an education qualification requirement
Details.Evaluations: You will be evaluated based on how well you meet the qualifications listed in this vacancy announcement. Your qualifications will be evaluated based on your application materials (e.g., resume, supporting documents), the responses you provide on the application questionnaire, and the result of the online assessments required for this position. You will be assessed on the following competencies (knowledge, skills, abilities, and other characteristics): Competencies: Reading, Judgment, Interaction & Reasoning The resume/documents you submit must support your responses to the online questionnaire. If your application contradicts or does not support your questionnaire responses, you will receive a rating of "not qualified" or "insufficient information" and you will not receive further consideration for this job. Your application package (resume, supporting documents, and responses to the questionnaire) will be used to determine your eligibility, qualifications, and quality ranking for this position. Please follow all instructions carefully. Errors or omissions may affect your rating or consideration for employment. APPRAISALS/AWARDS: Hiring Managers use objective methods and consider previous performance appraisals and awards in the selection process. Current Federal Civilian employees should list any relevant performance related rating and/or awards in your resume. BASIS OF RATING: The assessments for this job will also measure Knowledge, Skills and Abilities (KSA) as listed under Qualifications Your application will be rated under the Cut Point procedures based on the extent to which the quality, depth, and complexity of your experience and education relate to the qualification requirements. Additional points are not added for Veteran's Preference; however, Veteran's Preference is considered where applicable. Best Qualified Group: Candidates in this category possess exceptional skills and experience to exceed well above the minimum requirements Fully Qualified Group: Candidates in this category possess good skills and experience above the minimum requirements. Basically Qualified Group: Candidates in this category meet the minimum education and/or experience requirements. To be considered for this position, you must complete all required steps in the process. In addition to the application and application questionnaire, this position requires an online assessment. The online assessment measures critical general competencies required to perform the job. Overstating your qualifications and/or experience in your application materials or application questionnaire may result in your removal from consideration. Cheating on the online assessment may also result in your removal from consideration. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: ***THIS POSITION IS PART OF THE DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE PILOT PROGRAM.*** ***Please read this announcement in its entirety before applying.*** Under the DoD Pilot Program, there is no requirement to prepare a narrative statement specifically addressing the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs). However, to meet the minimum qualification requirements for this position, you must show that you possess the five Executive Core Qualifications within your resume -- not to exceed five pages. Your application must also include a narrative statement specifically addressing the mandatory technical qualifications not to exceed a total of two pages. http://www.opm.gov/ses/references/guidetoSESQuals_2012.pdf Each accomplishment should be clear, concise, and emphasize your level of responsibilities; the scope and complexity of the programs, activities, or services you managed; program accomplishments; policy initiatives undertaken; level of contacts; the sensitivity and criticality of the issues you addressed; and the results of your actions. You should use action oriented leadership words to describe your experience and accomplishments (e.g., Led the development and implementation of....) and quantify your experience wherever possible to demonstrate your accomplishments (e.g., number of employees supervised; size of budget managed; amount of money saved, etc.). ECQ 1 - Leading Change: This core qualification involves the ability to bring about strategic change, both within and outside the organization, to meet organizational goals. Inherent to this ECQ is the ability to establish an organizational vision and to implement it in a continuously changing environment. ECQ 2 - Leading People: This core qualification involves the ability to lead people toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals. Inherent to this ECQ is the ability to provide an inclusive workplace that fosters the development of others, facilitates cooperation and teamwork, and supports constructive resolution of conflicts. ECQ 3 - Results Driven: This core qualification involves the ability to meet organizational goals and customer expectations. Inherent to this ECQ is the ability to make decisions that produce high-quality results by applying technical knowledge, analyzing problems, and calculating risks. ECQ 4 - Business Acumen: This core qualification involves the ability to manage human, financial, and information resources strategically. ECQ 5 - Building Coalitions: This core qualification involves the ability to build coalitions internally and with other Federal agencies, State and local governments, nonprofit and private sector organizations, foreign governments, or international organizations to achieve common goals. MANDATORY TECHNICAL QUALIFICATIONS: All applicants must submit written statements (narrative format) of accomplishments that would satisfy the technical qualifications. You are required to respond to all of the technical qualifications. If you fail to do so, you will be rated as ineligible. Please limit your written statement to no more than 2 pages. Comprehensive experience at the executive or managerial level, indicating a broad understanding and sensitivity to current national security concerns and policies. Includes the ability to analyze and understand complex civilian personnel issues and present intellectual and practical solutions. Demonstrated ability to collaborate at the senior executive level with a wide variety of outside organizations such as the Congress, other federal agencies, private sector industry and special interest and advocacy groups, advocating, and expressing facts and ideas in a convincing manner, and negotiating with individuals and groups as well as developing an expansive professional network with senior level officials in other organizations, to identify the internal and external politics that impact the work of the organization. Demonstrated experience creating, developing and directing policies at the most senior levels of a large organization and knowledge of Federal and/or DoD civilian personnel policies, including recruiting, retention, compensation, and personnel management. Knowledge and demonstrated expertise of the statutory and regulatory framework for civilian personnel management, and with federal civilian personnel management policies, processes and legislative activities. DoD Joint Enterprise-Wide Experience Statement: In addition, DoD requires an Enterprise Perspective. This individual must have the ability to apply a broad point of view and an awareness and understanding of individual or organizational responsibilities in relation to DoD or government-wide strategic priorities is required. Executives must demonstrate ability to work with internal and external partners to support national security objectives. This perspective is typically gained through a variety of diverse work experiences. A separate narrative statement is not required. This information should be embedded within the application package (Resume and technical qualifications).

Details.JobSummary: The Principal Director, Civilian Personnel Policy (PD(CPP)) position is located in the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense (Personnel and Readiness), Office of the Secretary of Defense, and responsible for supporting the Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense (DASD(CPP)) in oversight and enforcement of DoD civilian personnel management policies.
Details.SubAgencyName: Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD) is the principal staff element of the Secretary of Defense in the exercise of policy development, planning, resource management, and program evaluation responsibilities. OSD includes the Offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of Defense, Under Secretaries of Defense, Assistant Secretaries of Defense, General Counsel and the Director of Administration and Management. This position is in the Senior Executive Service (SES), a small, elite group of top government leaders. SES members possess a diverse portfolio of experiences including strong skills to lead across organizations. As a Senior Executive, you will influence the direction of innovation and transformation of the federal government and lead the next generation of public servants.
MajorDuties: The Principal Director, Civilian Personnel Policy (PD(CPP)) advises and coordinates DoD's activities for the DASD(CPP) on such matters as the modernization of human resources systems, improved quality of HR information, and legislation affecting civilian HR operations and organizations at cabinet­-interdepartmental planning and policy meetings. Duties will also include but are limited to: Works closely with the Office of Personnel Management (OPM), the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Congress, and the other 23 Executive Departments and Federal agencies. Specific areas of responsibility include, but are not limited to: labor-management and employee relations; performance management; employment; classification, compensation; executive resource management; strategic human capital planning and evaluation; merit system principles; workforce and leadership development; civilian talent management; workplace violence; work life programs; DoD's Non-Appropriated Fund personnel system; the development, integration, modernization, and sustainment of the civilian HR management information technology systems; the expeditionary civilian program; and benefits and entitlements. Serves as the senior DoD subject matter expert in the above fields and directs senior staff in all assigned program areas. Directs the development and implementation of policies, programs, and regulations for the entire lifecycle of civilian HR functional areas and provides the Director and Deputy Director, Defense Civilian Personnel Advisory (DCPAS) Policy direction. Formulates Department-wide Human Resource Management (HRM) strategic plans, programmatic objectives, policies, standards, directives, and instructions through a subordinate policy staff of civilian personnel experts and directs and provides oversight to the DCPAS Director and Deputy on the same. Supports the DASD(CPP) in oversight and enforcement of DoD civilian personnel management policies. The incumbent reviews and analyzes DoD components' personnel programs to promote economy, improvement, and consistency in the application of DoD civilian personnel management policies and programs. Acts on behalf of the DASD(CPP) who is the delegated DoD CHCO on behalf of the USD(P&R). Advises and assists the DASD(CPP) in assigned responsibilities and functions and provides support to the DoD Components in the administration of civilian personnel policy and programs, as directed. Investigates and evaluates new approaches and developments within the human resources management field and conducts studies leading to the application of these practices to DoD-wide civilian personnel policies and programs Participates in the coordination of the annual review of Component civilian employment targets and plans. Supervises the development of innovative alternatives and new solutions to civilian work force management problems. Supervises the preparation of issue papers and decision documents for use by the USD(P&R), ASD(M&RA), and DASD(CPP). Provides oversight to the development and evaluation of the various DoD personnel demonstration projects; policies and programs for the employment of U.S. citizens in foreign areas; and provides guidance to the DoD Per Diem Travel and Transportation Allowance Committee on civilian travel, per diem, and relocation allowances. Directs the administration of executive personnel matters for the Department, including the Senior Executive Service, Senior Professionals, Highly Qualified Experts, and equivalent positions under OPM approved demonstration projects. Represents DoD during interaction contacts with appropriate segments of the Legislative, Executive, and Judicial Branches of the Federal Government, professional, special interest and public citizens groups, and the media (in coordination with the Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense ASD (Public Affairs) staff on civilian personnel matters. Represents the Department in meetings with senior officials of the DoD Components, the Office of Personnel Management, the Department of State, other Federal agencies, various national labor organizations, and Defense Department officials from other countries. Works with the Military Departments, Defense Agencies and Field Activities, members of Congress, Congressional staff members, high-level officials of Federal, state, and local government entities, and local and national officials of public service and other organizations interested in public personnel administration and human resources management.
Details.Education: There is no education requirement for this position.
Details.Requirements: You must be a U.S. citizen to qualify for this position. All newly appointed Career SES leaders must sign the Reassignment Rights Obligations Agreement as a condition of appointment into the SES. You must submit to a drug test and receive a negative drug test before you can be appointed into this position. Designated and/or Random Drug Testing required. In order to qualify for this position, you must be able to obtain a Top Secret security clearance. Submit resume and all other required documents online by 11:59 PM Eastern Standard Time on 04/27/2023 The individual selected will be required to file an 'Executive Branch Personnel Financial Disclosure Report (OGE-278) in accordance with the Ethics in Government Act of 1978. You will serve a one-year probationary period unless you have previously completed the probationary period in the SES. Please read the vacancy announcement in its entirety before applying.
Details.Evaluations: You will be evaluated on the quality and extent of your total accomplishments, experience, and education. Your application will be evaluated by a rating and ranking panel. Highly qualified candidates may undergo an interview and a reference check. The Office of the Secretary of Defense Executive Resources Board will review results and make recommendations on final selections to the appointing authority.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. The incumbent will be responsible for all matters pertaining to contingency plan development, plan review and assessment, collaboration, and global defense posture..
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The J-5 (Directorate for Strategy Plans and Policy) proposes strategies, plans, and policy recommendations to the CJCS (Chairman of the Joints Chiefs of Staff) to support the provision of "military advice" across the full spectrum of national security concerns to the President and other national leaders and to ensure those recommendations are informed by a larger strategic context coordinated with interagency and alliance partners, account for the view and requirements of the combatant commanders, and assess risk in executing the National Military Strategy.
MajorDuties: As a JOINT STRATEGIC PLANNER at the GS-0301-14 some of your typical work assignments may include: Being a recognized expert in formulating Joint Staff positions on the Contingency Planning Guidance (CPG), the Guidance for Employment of the Force (GEF), the Joint Strategic Campaign Plan (JSCP) and coordination of Global Defense Posture (GDP). Assisting in the preparation of Congressional testimony by the CJCS and other senior military members of the Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) on matters of national strategy, contingency plans, and global posture. Collaborating closely with the Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD), the Services, and the Combatant Commands (CCMD). The work performed will provide military decision makers with authoritative information forming the basis for decisions affecting current and future military strategy, plans, force employment, posture, and Joint Force options to mitigate strategic and military risk. Serving as a senior Joint Operational War planner, applying systematic analysis methods in order to assess CCMD war plans and global posture. Managing inputs and contributions to diverse strategy and plan development cycles and reviews for the Combatant Commands, Services, Defense Agencies, and other departments and agencies of the United States government and the Joint Staff as outlined in the Joint Strategic Campaign Plan and JCS Instruction, Management and Review of Campaign and Contingency Plans.

A "certification" letter should be on letterhead of the appropriate military branch of the service and contain (1) the military service dates including the expected discharge or release date; and (2) the character of service. OSD includes the immediate offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of Defense, Under Secretaries of Defense, Director of Defense Research and Engineering, Assistant Secretaries of Defense, General Counsel, Director of Operational Test and Evaluation, Assistants to the Secretary of Defense, Director of Administration and Management, and such other staff offices as the Secretary establishes to assist in carrying out assigned responsibilities.

This position is in the Excepted Service and does NOT convey eligibility to be converted to the Competitive Service. It is being recruited under 10 U.S.C. 1599f into the Cyber Excepted Service (CES) personnel system. If you are a current Federal Career/Career-Conditional employee, you will be placed on an Excepted appointment. This appointment does not confer eligibility to be non-competitively converted to an appointment in the competitive service. For more information see https://public.cyber.mil/cw/dod-cyber-excepted-service-ces/ Incumbents typical work assignments may include the following: Serves as the Program Manager of the Defense Industrial Base (DIB) Operations Directorate and as an advisor on cybersecurity, acquisition of Cybersecurity-as-a-Service, and cyber policies and procedures. Directs research based on the results of audits, inspections, management reviews, Congressional hearings, and other evaluations to isolate programmatic deficiencies and establishes long-range programs that contribute to more favorable and predictable outcomes. Coordinates and harmonizes DIB Cybersecurity program activities encompassing all missions and all echelons; near-term, mid-term, and long-term time frames across all theaters and all levels of conflict from peacetime/crisis operations through major conflict to support the warfighter. Serves on boards, committees, and other groups pertaining to DoD CIO functional areas, and represents the DCIO(CS) or DoD CIO on matters for all internal DoD, interagency and international cybersecurity forums.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: Only applicants who meet one of the employment authority categories below are eligible to apply for this job. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected. See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities. 30 Percent or More Disabled Veterans Current Department of Army Civilian Employees Current Department of Defense (DOD) Civilian Employee (non-Army) Domestic Defense Industrial Base/Major Range and Test Facilities Base Civilian Personnel Workforce Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan Land Management Workforce Flexibility Act Military Spouses, under Executive Order (E.O.) 13473 Non-Appropriated Fund Instrumentality (NAFI) Non-Department of Defense (DoD) Transfer People with Disabilities, Schedule A Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Spouse Preference (MSP) Eligible Reinstatement Veterans Employment Opportunity Act (VEOA) of 1998 In order to qualify, you must meet the experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes: developing detailed project plans, tasks, and/or schedules; identifying resource requirements, manpower and funding, to implement projects; developing tools to track progress throughout the life cycle of the projects; evaluating the status and progress of work accomplished in terms of quality, efficiency, and effectiveness in achieving objectives; and managing operational control over assigned projects in the privatized housing program. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-13). You will be evaluated on the basis of your level of competency in the following areas: Administration and Management Decision Support Project Management Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-13).

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position serves in the Housing & Capital Ventures section of the Office of the Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Army (Installations, Housing and Partnerships), Assistant Secretary of the Army (Installations, Energy and Environment) (ASA (IE&E)), in Arlington, VA.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Serve as program manager for housing related management decision execution packages (MDEPS).
Develop tools and methods to track progress throughout the life cycle of housing inventory.
Brief senior leadership, OSD, and Congressional staff on project status and significant developments.
Apply technical knowledge to ensure schedules and objectives are accomplished in accordance with established milestones.
Maintain productive interaction with all stakeholders.
Negotiates the investment of private capital in on-post housing.
Coordinate with privatized housing companies and senior leadership to implement private sector approaches to manage, construct, and renovate the on-post Housing inventory.
Develop strategies, procedures, and activities to accomplish program goals and objectives.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-13, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes: (1) applying analytical and evaluative methods and techniques to integrate research data into informed decision-making recommendations; (2) designing or developing new or improved work methods, management processes and/or program effectiveness and/or organizational productivity procedures; (3)making recommendations on substantive operating programs, planning, organizing, developing projects, and negotiating effectively with others to accept and implement recommendations; (4) knowledge of major manpower, personnel services issues, program goals and objectives in the sequence and timing of key events and milestones, roles of MAJCOMs, Forward Operating Agencies, Air Staff directorates and divisions, and methods of evaluating the effectiveness of strategic plans and requirements actions as related to key events; (5) providing interface between field staff, field agencies, cross-org Air staff elements, and AF/A1S through conferences, orientations and meetings. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in-­grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-13 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-14 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Knowledge of DoD and Air Force goals, objectives, and policies including knowledge of the relationship of the various Air Force entities involved in manpower, personnel, and services policies. 2. Knowledge of research and analysis techniques, problem resolution, and development of concrete action plans to solve problems. 3. Knowledge and skill in the application of Air Force workflow and task management directives, instructions, policies, procedures, and guidance. 4. Skill and ability to apply procedures, requirements, regulations, and policies related to specialized expertise in the work of the directorate, including the ability to maintain credibility with others on policy matters. 5. Ability to synthesize complex, and often competing, information and viewpoints to determine best course of action and advocate recommendations across the Air Staff and to senior Air Force leaders. 6. Ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing, negotiates complex issues, and maintains good working relationships. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.JobSummary: Click on "Learn more about this agency" button below to view Eligibilities being considered and other IMPORTANT information. The primary purpose of this position is to serve as Services Strategic Actions Officer of the Resources and Requirements Division, reporting to the Director of Services, Headquarters, United States Air Force. The incumbent is responsible for working on behalf of the Director (AF/A1S) on strategic, Congressional, and operational issues.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is: To fly, fight, and win...Airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Global Reach and Global Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do. Click here to view the AF Civilian Employment Eligibility Guide: 30 Percent or More Disabled Veterans AF DCIPS Interchange AF Internal Employee DoD Transfer (Excluding Air Force) EO 12721 Certain Former Overseas Employees EO 13473 Appointment of Certain Military Spouses Former Federal Employees (Reinstatement) Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan Land Management Employee Military Spouse Preference National Service (Peace Corps and VISTA) Non-AF DCIPS Interchange Non-Appropriated Fund Non-DoD Transfer Other (Interchange Agreements) People with Disabilities, Schedule A Veterans Employment Opportunities Act
MajorDuties: Contributes to AF/A1S processes, and senior leader support. Ensures inputs from across the AF/A1S enterprise are accurately and effectively integrated for appropriate AF/A1S processes. Assesses and assigns queries from staff and members of Congress and evaluates applicability and quality of responses. Serves as subject matter expert on administrative working groups to plan and develop strategies to address administrative issues and concerns.

At the time the active duty member applies for a civil position, he or she must submit a "certification" memo in lieu of a DD-Form 214, Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty. Active duty members applying for a civil service position without submitting a valid certification memo or DD-Form 214 with their application will render the member ineligible for the position. The certification memo must originate from the member's military service branch on official letterhead and contain the following: Name/Rank/Grade of Service Member Branch of Armed Forces Dates of Active Service (Start and End Date(s) Expected Date of Discharge/Release from Active Duty Terminal leave start date (if applicable) Expected character of service (honorable or general) and type of separation (i.e. separation or retirement) Must be certified within 120 days of anticipated discharge Signature by, or by direction of the adjutant, personnel office, unit commander, or higher headquarters commander. Note: The VOW Act provides tentative preference. If appointed, a DD Form-214 must be submitted upon receipt. Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Serve as senior Management Support Specialist for Civilian personnel with responsibility for assisting in the planning and executing of personnel and administrative programs. Serves as a lead for civilian personnel engaged in performance of personnel management and administration for the Assistant Secretary of the Army (ASA), Financial Management and Comptroller (FM&C) and Deputy Chief of Staff, G-8.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Exercise oversight of civilian personnel engaged in performance of personnel management and administration support for the ASA, FM C and G-8.

Provide expert advice on civilian personnel regulations and assists managers and employees in non-technical matters, refers appropriate technical matters, and performs Civilian Personnel Advisory Center (CPAC) liaison functions.
Coordinate with external points of contact in the CPAC and Headquarters Department of Army (HQDA).

Ensure determinations and decisions concerning major policy and courses of action are consistent with laws and regulations governing administration of civilian personnel and actual or probable impact on the workforce.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-13, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes: I have at least one full year of specialized experience at the GS-13 (or higher) grade level or equivalent in other pay systems (may have been obtained in the military, public or private sectors that includes: (1) having mastery of, and skill in applying workforce management and Force Development principles, concepts and practices in the area of formal and voluntary education, functional training and professional development; (2) knowledge is sufficient to serve as the AF focal point for guidance in developing and implementing education, training and professional developmental policy, competencies, and programs; (3) ability to identify and propose solutions to AF developmental problems that are broad, severe, and for which previous studies and established techniques are frequently inadequate; (4) developing and implementing effective metrics and control measures to measure progress and success of programs and adapt programs and policies as needed; (5) providing effective change management and strategic communication support to ensure success and acceptance of programs and policies. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in-­grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-13 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-14 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Knowledge of the laws, rules, and regulations governing workforce management and Force Development policy and programs (military and civilian). 2. Ability to manage several projects simultaneously and to lead and/or actively participate as contributing team member in AF or DoD-level working groups. 3. Skill in written and oral communication such that it influences decisions, outcomes, or opinions. 4. Ability to lead, present, and communicate with a diverse group of senior leaders as the lead action officer for Total Force Development projects, working groups and panels. 5. Knowledge of the concepts, principles, theories, and practices of strategic workforce management and development. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.JobSummary: Click on "Learn more about this agency" button below to view Eligibilities being considered and other IMPORTANT information. The primary purpose of this position is to develop/integrate Air Force ( AF) policy, programs, and procedures for developmental programs that are synchronized across the continuum of learning-education, training, developmental and experiential programs.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is: To fly, fight, and win...Airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Global Reach and Global Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do. Click here to view the AF Civilian Employment Eligibility Guide: 30 Percent or More Disabled Veterans AF DCIPS Interchange AF Internal Employee DoD Transfer (Excluding Air Force) EO 12721 Certain Former Overseas Employees EO 13473 Appointment of Certain Military Spouses Former Federal Employees (Reinstatement) Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan Land Management Employee Military Spouse Preference National Service (Peace Corps and VISTA) Non-AF DCIPS Interchange Non-Appropriated Fund Non-DoD Transfer Other (Interchange Agreements) People with Disabilities, Schedule A Veterans Employment Opportunities Act
MajorDuties: Develop Air Force Development policy and programs to meet AF requirements and implement OSD/DoD/OPM strategies for competency-based workforce development. Develop policy to meet Air Force requirements/strategies and implement OSD/DoD/OPM directives for Force Development - training, education, and professional development. Analyze, evaluate, and develop leadership framework, program objectives, functional requirements, operating methods and new and proposed regulatory guidelines to advance the Air Force goal of a competency based workforce. Support organizations and senior level governance structures and working groups to include, but not limited to, the Lemay Doctrine Center, Air University (AU), USAFA, Functional Managers (FM), Development Team (DT), the Force Development Panels/Developmental Education Boards, Leadership Program Selection Boards, Air Force Learning Committee, and the DoD Chief Learning Officer Council (D-CLOC), consisting of component representatives and Senior Executive Service (SES) members and General Officers (GO).

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-14, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes (1) collaborating and coordinating efforts of DoD-wide business improvements to achieve strategic management priorities and business outcomes reported to Office of Management and Budget (OMB) and Congress; (2) knowledge of national defense planning - overall planning objectives, timing and sequence of key planning events, processes, procedures; (3) identifying issues and problems on his/her own initiative and to formulate and conduct analyses and present recommendations toward the resolution of the issues and source documents of key organizations; (4) expert knowledge of national defense planning - overall planning objectives, timing and sequence of key planning events, processes, procedures and source documents of key organizations; includes knowledge of executive and congressional directives and guidance regarding Defense or Service future direction and major strategic issues. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in-­grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-14 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-15 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Comprehensive knowledge of Department of Defense Chief Management Officer; Department of Air Force policy, procedures, SPPBE construct and Air Force corporate governance; methods for effecting AF-wide policy and process improvement to include support business case analysis and documented business process reengineering results to ensure most effective and efficient Air Force business operations. 2. Extensive knowledge in planning and execution of AF-wide business improvement and change management activities that span process, organizational and supporting business system changes. This includes ability to gather, assemble, analyze facts, draw conclusions, conduct analysis, devise recommended solutions, and package the entire process in briefings, papers, or reports suitable for top management use and decision-making. 3. In-depth knowledge in continuous process improvement and Air Force corporate structure bodies and processes. Includes ability to develop strategic priorities and performance gaps and development plans and countermeasures to close those gaps. 4. Skilled in researching, analyzing and developing broad and far-reaching strategic and long-range plans within the assigned area of responsibility. 5. Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing. 6. Knowledge of in one or more of the following functional specialties: finance/budget, logistics, civil engineering, manpower/personnel, defense health programs, communications/information technology, acquisition/contracting, services, or planning/programming. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Knowledge of safety and security regulations, practices, and procedures. Ability to plan, organize, and direct the functions and staff of a small to medium sized organization. Knowledge of the Department of Defense Joint Capabilities Integration Development System (JCIDS) and service program goals and objectives, the sequence and timing of key operational events and milestones, and methods of evaluating the effectiveness of planning actions as related to actual events. Knowledge of the relationship of the various military entities involved in overall planning and execution of military operations and evaluations and the methods in which the SPPBE and JCIDS processes supports them. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Global Reach and Global Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do. MajorDuties: Plans, organizes, performs, and directs the resourcing, acquisition, and sustainment (RAS) activities for the Air Force Special Warfare Directorate (A3S), ensuring that these activities comply with legal and regulatory requirements and meets customer needs. Exercises supervisory personnel management responsibilities. Represents AF/A3S to a variety of command and functional area organizations. Serves as lead integrator across AFSPECWAR for RAS and highlights opportunities, disconnects, and offsets in the Air Force and DoD corporate process. Manages, coordinates, and integrates AFSPECWAR mission and program requirements through collaboration with Headquarters Air Force (HAF) staff and MAJCOMs to organize, train, and equip AFSPECWAR forces.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Provides continuity in the effective oversight and coordination of joint initiatives developed by the separate, but interrelated divisions within the directorate.
Accelerates and strengthens the joint interoperability and integration of Combatant Commander's war-fighting capabilities within JCO (Joint Counter Office).
Determines impact on war-fighting programs resulting from joint service programmatic changes.
Receives, analyzes, and processes Joint requirement documents through the Joint Capabilities Integration and Development System (JCIDS) from authorized joint requirement organizations and processes.

Serves as one of the directorate?s integrators for JCO?s participation in the Joint Strategic Planning System (JSPS) and provides visibility of those equities within the Army Program Objective Memorandum (POM) strategy.

Assesses problems and issues associated with development and integration of operations and systems to include technology readiness integration and timeline challenges as it relates to joint interoperability.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will coordinate efforts related to planning, programming, and budgeting of ship support programs.
You will validate and assess maritime ship support requirements to develop Program Objective Memoranda (POM).
You will analyze ship support readiness requirements and provide recommendations based on the level of acceptable risk and the impact of insufficient funding.
You will analyze the impact of resource sponsor funding decisions and budget reviews for ship support readiness requirements and operational availability.
You will manage and update requirement data within Navy?s Program Budget Information System (PBIS) database.
You will develop and refine ship support readiness policies in accordance with program requirements.
You will review ship support budget exhibits to ensure they are consistent with programming/budgeting decisions.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a MANAGEMENT ANALYST in the ADMINISTRATIVE DIVISION, FMA of ASN.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will conduct studies of employee/organizational efficiency and productivity to possible recommended changes or improvements in organization, staffing, work methods, policies and procedures.

You will measure the effectiveness, efficiency and productivity of administrative civilian personnel programs and work with Human Resource Office (HRO) to provide support across the full spectrum of Personnel Management functions to leadership.

You will advise managers and senior leaders on civilian personnel functions in a customer-centric environment for Financial Management and Comptroller (FMC) and will ensure the laws, regulations, standards, policies.

You will assist in the design and conduct of special human resources studies that develop customer specific options to resolve long-term human resources problems or anticipate future human capital needs.
You will be responsible for developing and implementing succession planning strategies; that identify and develop future leaders within the organization; create and maintain a talent management plan.

You will will prioritize objectives in support of organizational business transformation initiatives; conduct HR analytics strategy, policies, and guidance; and collects, aggregates, analyzes, and reports on a wide variety of data.
You will be responsible developing and implementing strategies to manage the organization's talent, track workforce demographics, and measure the effectiveness of talent management programs.
You will conduct workforce planning analyses to ensure that the organization has the right talent to meet its current and future needs.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a Management Analyst coordinating and supporting integrated capability requirements development addressing one or more capabilities that cannot be delivered by a single program of record. This position is in the Pentagon, Arlington, VA in the DNI/DDNI OPNAV SUPPORT STAFF.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will focus Navy efforts to ensure requirements traceability from high level down through detailed performance specifications in individual programs deliver results to achieve the envisioned capability.
You will coordinate capability-specific requirements with those supporting, or interdependent with, other mission or capability areas.

You will ensure synchronization with Naval Operational Architecture (NOA) requirements and Joint All Domain Command and Control (JADC2) capability development efforts, with particular emphasis on sensing and targeting needs for Long Range Fires.
You will coordinate Navy participation and substantive integration in working groups and ensure Navy and naval equities are accurately represented in joint documents and other products.
You will provide support to the integrated analysis plan and science/technology efforts designed to most effectively close identified gaps.

You will coordinate among Navy stakeholders for participation and tasker responses and ensure Navy integration in joint experiments and assessments is aligned with the NOA capabilities planned and implemented through Project Over-match.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: US Citizens In order to qualify, you must meet the experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes: assisting management with communication and/or coordination of energy plans with stakeholders consistent with policy and leadership guidance; collaborating with principal staff to establish and assess energy program goals, priorities, resources, staffing, and workload requirements; monitoring energy and water technology and associated cyber resilience programs to ensure program goals and objectives are met consistent with commitments and policy, as well as measurable performance criteria; and conducting reviews to elevate key issues for resolution in programs such as: energy and water emerging technologies, energy and water monitoring and management technologies, energy and water data science, and cyber resilience of energy and water technologies. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-14).

Details.JobSummary: This is a Direct Hire Authority (DHA) solicitation utilizing the DHA for Certain Personnel of the DoD Workforce to recruit and appoint qualified candidates to positions in the competitive service. About the Position: Serves as a Program Director/Manager for the Office of the Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Army (Energy and Sustainability), located in Arlington, VA.
Details.SubAgencyName: Office of the Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Army (Energy and Sustainability)
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Provide program oversight, strategic planning, policy recommendations, and establish goals and objectives for energy initiatives.
Assist the Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Army (Energy and Sustainability) in their role as the Army?s Senior Energy Executive (SEE).
Coordinate programs from installations to Headquarters, Department of the Army to the Office of the Secretary of Defense with full authority for management decisions related to program initiatives.

Evaluate technologies for Army installation-applicability of renewable and carbon-free energy, and energy and water efficiency, resilience, security, energy and water generation, distribution, storage, controls, and management.
Communicate with internal and external stakeholders, in written and oral formats, to ensure knowledge transfer and technology adoption.
Implement programs that may span several years, involve sensitive issues, and be subject to Congressional and/or media scrutiny.
